CalibrationCurve.description:
A calibration measured as pairs, such as valve opening time against volume per pulse, with its linear fit.

The fit is made in Python when the curve is written; a rig whose configuration points a
CalibratedPulse at the file reads `linear_fit` and `pulse_gap_ms`, never the points.

calibratedAt.description: When the calibration was measured, in UTC.
calibratedAt.title: CalibratedAt

machineName.description: Name of the machine the calibration was measured on. LoadRewardLine refuses a valve calibration from any other machine.
machineName.title: MachineName

xName.description: Name of the quantity the rig controls.
xName.title: XName

points.description: Measured pairs, kept as the record of what was weighed.
points.title: Points

pulseGapMs.description: Off-to-on time between the pulses of each sample, in milliseconds; a rig fires at the same gap.
pulseGapMs.title: PulseGapMs

linearFit.description: The line fitted to the points, which a rig plans with.

payloadPath.description: Relative path of a file a consumer still needs alongside the points, such as a gamma LUT bitmap.
payloadPath.title: PayloadPath

CalibrationCurve.title: CalibrationCurve

CalibrationPoint.description: One measured pair of a calibration curve.

x.description: The value the rig controls, in the unit of the x axis.
x.title: X

y.description: The measured value, in the unit of the y axis.
y.title: Y

DispenseCalibration.description:
What an experiment repository commits as `config/<dispenser>-calibration.yml`.

A calibration workflow deserialises it with the Core `DeserializeFromYaml` and runs the
procedure; the balance port is set on the workflow at run time.

procedure.description: What to fire and how to weigh it.
procedure.title: Procedure

DispenseCalibration.title: DispenseCalibration

DispenseProcedure.description:
Settings of the dispense calibration: fire known sizes, weigh the gain, write a CalibrationCurve.

Run by a calibration workflow; the fit is done afterwards in Python and written into the CalibrationCurve.

samples.description: Sizes to measure, each fired and weighed in turn.
samples.title: Samples

primingPulses.description: Pulses fired before the baseline weighing to fill the line.
primingPulses.title: PrimingPulses

primingSize.description: Size of the priming pulses; the largest sample size when unset.
primingSize.title: PrimingSize

densityGPerMl.description: Density used to turn the weighed grams into microlitres. Water = 1.0.
densityGPerMl.title: DensityGPerMl

settleWindow.description: Consecutive stable readings, after the last pulse, before a weight is taken.
settleWindow.title: SettleWindow

weighTimeoutS.description: Fail if the balance has not settled within this time, in seconds.
weighTimeoutS.title: WeighTimeoutS

DispenseProcedure.title: DispenseProcedure

DispenseSample.description: One size to measure: the dispenser fires `repeats` times at it and the gain is weighed once.

size.description: The size to fire, in the procedure's x unit: milliseconds for a valve, steps for a pump.
size.title: Size

repeats.description: Pulses fired at this size before the gain is weighed.
repeats.title: Repeats

pulseGapMs.description: Off-to-on time between consecutive pulses, in milliseconds; long enough for the valve to seat.
pulseGapMs.title: PulseGapMs

DispenseSample.title: DispenseSample

LinearFit.description:
A straight line fitted to a curve's points: y = slope * x + intercept, valid from `min_x` to `max_x`.

For a valve, x is the pulse width in ms and y the volume per pulse in ul; a rig plans pulses only
inside the range.

slope.description: y per unit of x, such as ul per ms of pulse width.
slope.title: Slope

intercept.description: y at x = 0, in the unit of y.
intercept.title: Intercept

minX.description: Smallest x the fit is valid for, such as the shortest pulse width measured.
minX.title: MinX

maxX.description: Largest x the fit is valid for, such as the longest pulse width measured.
maxX.title: MaxX

LinearFit.title: LinearFit

A serial balance read by the platform's dispense calibration through `OpenRigs.Devices:SerialBalance.bonsai`.

Extends `SerialDevice` with the balance's protocol.
